packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-12 - unverified image-only reading (first reader)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of this text.
Rule note: I ran one `ls` on the three packet directories to learn the image filenames; that listing showed that packet.json exists. I did not open packet.json or anything else.

== image-001.jpg (overview, reduced) ==
Layout survey (observation): a narrow parchment strip (c. 10.5 cm long by c. 0.6-0.8 cm high against the scale at left) sitting in the gutter of an opened printed book; the printed blackletter text of the host book runs at 90 degrees below it and is not part of the fragment. The strip is a binding guard: only two lines of manuscript text are visible along it, upright in this frame, in a small dark gothic book hand with many abbreviations. The two lines are broken into four segments separated by blank intervals (tentative: the intervals are intercolumnar spaces/margins, so the strip may cut across more than one column; or the gaps are where the strip passes under sewing). One red stroke touches a capital in the right-most segment. No rubrics, running titles, or glosses visible; a crop this tight cannot show the layout.
Reading at overview scale (to be checked against the tiles below):
image-001 seg.1 l.1: re misit; q(uod)? dya(bolus)? seminauit
image-001 seg.1 l.2: zizania s(cilicet) h(e)reses (et) errores suo(s)
image-001 seg.2 l.1: ep(?) ...  ho(m)i(n)e gaudiu(m) ad audiendu(m)
image-001 seg.2 l.2: (et) sta(?) (et) ...on ad cru. q(uod)? q've h(abe)t v
image-001 seg.3 l.1: [upper line mostly hidden under the fold] ... i(n) ... 
image-001 seg.3 l.2: v(er)ba ad eliciendu(m)? lac expri(m)?
image-001 seg.4: see image-002

== image-002.jpg (tile, right-most segment) ==
image-002 l.1: ne g(e)n(er)a(?)ꝝ / gñaꝝ? v? adulatoꝝ (adulatorum) . [capital touched/crossed with red] Phy(si)ce? / Th...ic e? d̃
image-002 l.2: [first words cut by the lower edge of the strip: only tops of minims] ... lucratiua? [capital I with red stroke] I(te)m i(n) p(ro)ce(?)
Note: l.1 "adulatoꝝ" is secure; the word before it begins with g and ends in the -rum sign. The word after the point has a red horizontal stroke through its first letter (rubricator's touch, not a deletion - tentative).

== image-003.jpg (tile, third segment; its right edge overlaps image-002 "ne g...") ==
A vertical ruling/prick line stands just left of the text and another before "ne g...", i.e. these are column or text-block boundaries (observation); the area left of the first ruling is blank parchment (margin or intercolumn).
image-003 l.1 (upper half of the letters cut away by the fold; a red horizontal stroke through the middle of the line and a red paraph-like vertical stroke at its start): ...z? [red stroke] ap(?)u . xxx? ... e/c? i(n) t(er)cio? p(ri)me? / pu(n)c(to)?
image-003 l.2: v(er)ba ad h(oc)? eliciendu(m) lac exp(ri)m(?)ꝫ   [reading notes: "v̄ba" secure; then "ad" + a letter like h or ħ with a hook, then "eliciendū" (could be read as one word "adh..eliciendū"); "lac" secure; last word "exp" with superscript stroke + minims + final -ꝫ/-z: exp(ri)mit? / exp(ri)m(er)e? / expun(g)ꝫ?]
image-003 l.3: [only the tips of ascenders of a third line show at the lower edge of the strip]

== image-004.jpg (tile, second segment; left edge overlaps the end of segment 1: "...auit" / "...s suo(s)") ==
A vertical ruling stands between the end of segment 1 and the start of this segment (observation; tentative: column boundary).
image-004 l.1: q̄? (que/quod?) filius? ho(m)i(ni)s? g(ra)ti(a)m? / gaudiu(m)? [one short word, looks like "aꝫ"/"hꝫ"] ad audiendu(m)   [upper part of the line slightly rubbed; "ad audiendū" fairly secure]
image-004 l.2: ⁊ (et) sta(?) ⁊ (et) assu(?) . ad cru(?). / eru(?). Sꝫ (Sed) q̃ve? h(abe)t . v   [the two words after the first "et" are joined by a second Tironian et written through; "ad cru." or "ad eru." with a point after, i.e. abbreviated by suspension; then capital S + ꝫ = Sed (or "Q(uod)" - the form is a large round capital with -ꝫ); "q̃ve"/"q̃re" with abbreviation stroke; "h̃t"; line ends with ". v"]

== image-005.jpg (tile, first/left-most segment of the image-001 face; right edge overlaps image-004 start) ==
A vertical ruling stands left of the text (blank parchment to its left) and another after the line ends (observation). A rust-brown stain crosses the middle.
image-005 l.1: re misit, Sꝫ (Sed) dya(bo)l(u)s? sup(er)?seminauit   ["re" = end of a word begun on the lost line above; after "dya" a superscript sign then a short abbreviated element before "seminauit", partly under the stain: either "dyab(o)l(u)s seminauit" or "dya(bolus) sup(er)seminauit"]
image-005 l.2: zizania s(cilicet) h(e)reses (et) errores suo(s)   [secure except the final word "suo(s)"/"sico"]

Connected sense across the first face is NOT established: the four segments are two-line slices of what look like separate columns or of one long-line page interrupted by blank intervals; I give them in left-to-right order only.

== image-006.jpg (overview, reduced, second view) ==
Observation: the same or a similar guard strip seen from the other opening of the book (scale now at right, host print rotated the other way). Here THREE lines of manuscript are visible, in four segments separated by vertical rulings and blank intervals; a red initial (two lines high, square, at the start of the third segment's lower line) and several red-touched capitals. Same hand as image-001 (tentative). Reading at overview scale, to be checked against tiles:
image-006 seg.A: ...licet ... corp(or)i . Quod d / bem(us) eu(m) seq(ui) sp(irit)uali(ter) . Qu... sequi(mur) / cu(m) ip(s)e nos mon(et) dice(n)s .
image-006 seg.B: deu(m)? . [red-touched] Unde? Jacob(us) . Co(n)fi(te)mi(ni) al / terut(ru)m p(e)cc(at)a v(est)ra . Qui(n)ta? q(uod) debe
image-006 seg.C: vio . Jo(hannes)? offi(ciu)m incipit . Ecce / [red initial] Exiit q(ui) seminat (et)c. Sup(er)
image-006 seg.D: q(ui) vult? bibere (et)c. Ho(c)? eius? genui(?) ... / dendo . (et) a bono i(n) co(n)uiuio g(ra)c(i)as

== image-007.jpg (tile, segment A, left end of the image-006 face) ==
Ruled frame visible: vertical ruling left and right of the text, horizontal rulings under each line.
image-007 l.1 (upper half of letters cut by the strip edge): [illegible minims] ...licet? illi? corp(or)i . [capital] Quod d
image-007 l.2: bem(us) eu(m) seq(ui) sp(irit)uali(ter) . [capital] Qu(onia)m? / Qui(a)? sequi(mur)?   ["bem9" continues "d" of l.1 = d|bemus, tentative "debemus" with "de" abbreviated as "d"; "eū seq̊ sp̄uali" secure; last word "seqūn"/"sequī" with stroke]
image-007 l.3: cu(m) ip(s)e nos mon(et)? dice(n)s . [red-touched capital, cut by lower edge] ...   ["moın" - four minims after mo-, read "monet"/"mouit"?]

== image-008.jpg (tile, segment B; left edge overlaps image-007 "Quod d / sequi...") ==
Vertical ruling at left of this text block, preceded by a narrow blank interval after segment A (observation; tentative: A and B are adjacent columns). Lines here sit level with A's l.1-2. A small pink paper patch covers part of l.1.
image-008 l.1: deu(m)? / dem(us)? [patch covers c. 1-2 letters] . [capital, lower part only, with red] Unde? / [..]ida? [red-stroked J] Jacob(us) . [red-touched C] Co(n)fitemi(ni) al   ["Jacob9" secure; "Cōfitei"/"Cōfitem̄i" with strokes; line ends "al"]
image-008 l.2: terut(ru)m p(e)cc(at)a (et)c.? / v(est)ra? . [red-filled capital] Q(ui)nta? / Q(uar)ta? g° (ergo?) / q(uod)? debe   ["terutr̄ū pc̄ca" secure; the next sign is Tironian-et-like + c with stroke; then a round red-filled capital followed by ".ınta"/"uıta"; then g or q with superscript o; "debe" at line end, word continues on the lost next line]
image-008 l.3: [tops of ascenders only, at lower edge]

== image-009.jpg (tile, segment C; right edge overlaps image-010 start) ==
In the blank interval to the left of this block there is a tiny marginal note in ink, two or three letters: "Ju"? / "In"? (marginal addition, unread).
image-009 l.0: [bases of letters of a line above, cut by the upper edge]
image-009 l.1: vio . [red-stroked I/J] Io / Jo(hannes)? / I(de)o? offi(ciu)m incipit . [red-touched capital] Eccl(esi)e? / Ecce?   ["vio" = end of a word begun on the previous line; "offm̄ incipit" secure; final word begins with red-touched E/C and has ascenders with a stroke]
image-009 l.2: [large red initial, at least 2 lines high, square body with an inner ornament and a red vertical bar on its right; cut by the lower edge; could be E] xiit / Xiit q(ui) seminat (et)c. [red-touched S] Sup(er)   ["q̃ seminat ⁊c̃" secure; "Xiit"/"xut" four minims after x, i.e. tentatively the lemma "[E]xiit qui seminat etc."]
Tentative interpretation: a new section opening with a red initial and a short lemma ended by "etc.", followed by "Super ..." (commentary or citation); this is the best anchor on the leaf.

== image-010.jpg (tile, segment D, right end of the image-006 face) ==
Vertical rulings at both sides of the text block.
image-010 l.0: [bases of a line above, cut]
image-010 l.1: q(ui) vult? / q(ui)lib(et)? bibe(re)? (et)c. [capital with flourish] Ho(c)? / Ho(mo)? eius genui? / ge(n)tiu(m)? cre   [first word "qͥ"; second has v/l/b + superscript; "bibe"/"sibe" + "⁊c̃"; "eius" secure; "cre" continues in l.2]
image-010 l.2: dendo . (et) p(ro)? dono? / bono? i(n)carnac(i)o(n)is g(ra)c(i)as   ["cre|dendo" secure; after the point a Tironian et then a p-like letter with a crossed descender; "īcarnacōis grãs" fairly secure]
image-010 l.3: [tops of ascenders and abbreviation strokes only, cut by the lower edge]

== image-011.jpg (overview, reduced, third view) ==
Observation: inside of a book board (scale along the bottom, c. 22 cm). The pastedown is a leaf of PRINTED German text in two columns, set sideways (rotated 90 degrees), with hand-added red and green initials and red paraphs - this is print, not manuscript, and I have not transcribed it. The manuscript item here is a small parchment scrap at the top right corner under the turn-in (c. 3.5 cm wide), carrying two lines of ink text plus traces of a third, upright in this frame, with red-touched capitals. Further manuscript-looking traces (red marks, ink strokes) run down the extreme right edge in the gutter, too narrow to read at this scale and not covered by a tile. Tentative: the corner scrap is in a rounder, larger hand than the guard strips of image-001/006 and may come from a different leaf or a different manuscript.

== image-013.jpg (tile, left part of the corner scrap) ==
Blank parchment (margin) to the left of the text; text begins about one third of the way across.
image-013 l.1: [red-touched Tironian et] (et) medicat(ur)? / meditat(ur)? / mediator? [virgule] sui nece / nocte ...   [continues in image-012]
image-013 l.2: ...ierit? / reru(m)? d(eu)s [capital D heavily touched with red] Daemo(n)... / D[.]aemoꝝ   [continues in image-012]
image-013 l.3: [only two or three ink flecks at the lower edge]

== image-012.jpg (tile, right part of the corner scrap; left edge overlaps image-013 "sui ne..." / "...emoꝝ") ==
A crack/overlap in the parchment runs vertically through the right third; red offsets and flecks.
image-012 l.1 (upper part of letters cut by the leather turn-in): sui nece? / nocte? cu(m)? / ei(us)? c..at... [illegible beyond the crack]
image-012 l.2: [D]aemoꝝ (-orum; i.e. demonioꝝ? / daemonum?) sui? / fui? dei [red-touched capital, L or I or Z-like with a stroke above] Letat(ur)? / Iactat(ur)? [after the crack:] ...ctat(ur)9 / -tan(tur)?  then a 9-shaped sign (-us or a punctuation flourish) and one more cut letter
image-012 l.3: [tops of letters only: a round letter, an ascender pair (ll?), red flecks] [illegible]

== Selected / unread / limitations (packet-12) ==
- Selected: every visible manuscript line on the two guard-strip faces (image-001 with tiles 002-005; image-006 with tiles 007-010) and the corner scrap (011 with tiles 012-013). There is no span of ten connected lines anywhere: the strips preserve 2-3 lines per segment, and the segments are separated by rulings and blank intervals, so they are probably slices across several columns (or across both leaves of a bifolium) and NOT continuous prose from one segment to the next. Do not join segment ends to the next segment's start.
- Most secure phrases for a later match (each within one segment, two consecutive lines):
  (a) "...re misit, Sed dya... [super?]seminauit / zizania s(cilicet) hereses et errores suo(s)"
  (b) "...v(er)ba ad [h..] eliciendu(m) lac exp..."
  (c) "...adulatoru(m). ..." / "... I(te)m in p(ro)ce..."
  (d) "... Quod d|bemus eu(m) sequi sp(irit)uali(ter). Qu... sequi... / cu(m) ip(s)e nos mon.. dicens."
  (e) "... Jacobus. Confitemi(ni) al|terutru(m) p(e)cc(at)a ... Q..nta .. debe..."
  (f) "...vio. Io .. offi(ciu)m incipit. E... / [red initial] xiit q(ui) seminat etc. Sup(er)..."
  (g) "... bibe.. etc. Ho.. eius ... cre|dendo. et ... dono incarnac(i)o(n)is gr(aci)as"
  The expansions in (d)-(g) are mine from the abbreviations visible; alternatives are given line by line above.
- Uncertain: whether image-001 and image-006 show the two faces of one strip or two different strips; the order of segments; the relation of the corner scrap (image-011/012/013) to the strips.
- Unread: cut top and bottom lines on every segment (only bases or tips survive); the tiny marginal note left of segment C in image-009; the manuscript traces down the gutter edge in image-011; the printed host texts (deliberately not transcribed).
- Suggested: a tile of the gutter edge at the right of image-011; lifting views of the strips to expose the cut lines; a tile of the marginal note in image-009.
- This is an unverified image reading.
